newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cemig stake sale seen as "de-facto" privatization.
newsitem.headline: Cemig stake sale seen as "de-facto" privatization.

text.p: While only a one-third stake in Cemig goes on the auction block today, the sale is actually a "de-facto" privatization that will show the company to be a gem of Brazil's electrical sector, analysts said.

Market analysts said Cemig, a well-run integrated power firm owned by Minas Gerais state, is likely to gain in value once it gains a strategic foreign partner via the long-awaited selloff on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
The sale is set for 0900 local/1200 GMT at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
Four foreign-led consortia and local electric company Copel are prequalified to bid but only one group is expected to present an offer, according to financial daily Gazeta Mercantil.

The newspaper quoted BNDES Vice President Jose Pio Borges as saying only a group comprised of U.S.-based AES Corp and Southern Electric and a fund created by local bank Opportunity plans to present an offer.
Officials at BNDES could not be reached immediately to confirm the report.
But stock exchange officials said only one consortia had registered for the sale and observers said the firm was expected to bid the minimum price.
BNDESPar, the investment arm of BNDES, has set a base price of 60.37 reais per 1,000 shares for debentures convertible to Cemig common stock.
The auction, intended to gain a strategic partner for the firm, is slated for 0900 local/1200 gmt on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
Borges was quoted as saying other groups have decided not to bid because of the tough requirements set forth in the bid specifications for the sale.
"Pacific Corporation, one of the prequalified firms, desisted from the auction because it wanted more time to analyze the deal," he was quoted as saying.
He also said the base price also appears to have scarred off other potential bidders.
Cemig's common ended flat Tuesday in Sao Paulo at 48.00 reais while its preferred, or non-voting share, dropped 1.21 percent to close at 48.80 reais ahead of the sale.
BNDES and Minas Gerais state officials said they had managed to knock down late Tuesday the latest court challenges to the sale so that the long-delayed auction could proceed.
The voting stake in Cemig was originally slated to be auctioned late last year but has been repeatedly delayed.
